body:
Thanks for the details - can you summarize the change you're looking for? It's not clear from your description.

Also, if you could provide an example of the code plus the output you see from ESLint that you think is incorrect, that would help a lot.

Please check out the branch on my fork and run tests.

https://github.com/jrencz/eslint/blob/jrencz/issue/comment/tests/lib/rules/no-multi-spaces.js#L49-51

I'll be happy to do that. I'd still appreciate it if you could provide the info I've asked for in my previous comment. It will help all contributors understand what you're asking for, and that increases the possibility that someone will contribute a change.

Ok, so summing things up:

I'd like those 3 examples 

```
(function foo(a,/* b,*/ c){})
(function foo(a, /*b, */c){})
(function foo(a, b/*, c*/){})
```

not to rise `Multiple spaces found after ','.` in rule `no-multi-spaces`. The first 2 now do. The third does not.

I have seen this behavior too.

These will also trigger it:

``` javascript
function foo(a,/* b, */c){}
function foo(a,/*b,*/c){}
```

`Multiple spaces found after ','. (no-multi-spaces)`

I can take a look at this over the weekend.
Also, looking at your use case specifically @jrencz you might benefit from my [unparam](/gcochard/unparam) module regardless of this bug being fixed.

These new tests are failing:

``` javascript
(function(a,/* b, */c){})
(function(a,/*b,*/c){})
(function(a, /*b,*/c){})
(function(a,/*b,*/ c){})
(function(a, /*b,*/ c){})
```

These new tests are passing:

``` javascript
(function(/*a, b, */c){})
(function(/*a, */b, c){})
(function(a, b/*, c*/){})
(function(a, b/*,c*/){})
(function(a, b /*,c*/){})
(function(a/*, b ,c*/){})
(function(a /*, b ,c*/){})
```

Looks like it's only due to "middle" arguments.
I'll have a PR shortly.

issue.title: Fix: no-multi-spaces should allow comments (fixes #1659)

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
Comments offset the tokens for function params, but are not taken into
account when checking for spaces. This fixes that issue by adding the
comment's range to the token's range. Fixes #1659

body: @gcochard Thanks for the suggestion but unparam is not quite what will be useful for Angular DI pattern. I'd lie to have unused params detected statically. ESLint is probably a good tool to build such a detector but that's quite different case from the one I reported.
I don't think this is worth "fixing". :-1:. To me, `no-multi-spaces` is not really about the space characters, but about the positioning.

I disagree. I would say that commenting params out is a good thing. I have done this and Eslint has incorrectly flagged my code as having too many spaces when in reality there are none. Requirejs-style dependency injection is a good use case.

A commented-out parameter should have been deleted. Comments are for humans, not for disabling code (or god forbid, having some magic effect). If you're only doing it temporarily during development, you should either not run a linter yet or ignore those linter warnings.
It's still a bug. What if I were to put the expected type of parameter in the inline comment block? It's not in the jsdoc style, but it's still useful documentation.
I haven't really thought about this before but it's even better reason to fix this than mine.

Whether or not doing this is good coding practice really isn't relevant to this issue. The rule designed to detect multiple spaces is incorrectly reporting a comment as spaces. That's a bug in the rule that should be fixed.

This bug is not limited to function parameters.

``` js
 var a,/* b,*/c;

 var foo = [1,/* 2,*/3];

 var bar = {a: 1,/* b: 2*/c: 3};
```

``` sh
foo.js
  1:5   error  Multiple spaces found after ','  no-multi-spaces
  3:12  error  Multiple spaces found after ','  no-multi-spaces
  5:15  error  Multiple spaces found after ','  no-multi-spaces
```

I’m not sure if the current implementation of this rule is a good approach to correctly detect all occurrences of multiple spaces (see #1603). Maybe we should rewrite this rule to fix both issues.
I was thinking the same thing. Using tokens to do this seems like the wrong approach.

Definitely, seems like using source lines might be less of a hack. One thing this does bring up though is whether multiple spaces inside of comments should be ignored.

I would vote yes on this, but it might be good to make it an option. I can refactor my pr today or tomorrow.
Yeah, I think comments are an exception.
